request: Build the browser Minesweeper described in docs/SPEC.md, from scratch: the repository holds only the brief. Read the whole spec before planning. Its interfaces -- the exports of src/game/engine.ts, the page's element ids and attributes, the URL parameters and the npm scripts -- are a contract other code relies on, so follow them exactly; everything else is yours to design. Sound is synthesised with the Web Audio API and animations respect reduced motion, as the spec says. Write unit tests for the game rules and Playwright tests that drive the page. The work is done when npm run check passes, and npm run test:e2e passes against the production build, as separate gates.

task.title: Write unit tests for game rules
task.action: Create tests/engine.test.ts (or src/game/__tests__/engine.test.ts) covering all section-2 rules using deterministic layout-based boards. Each test title carries its requirement id in brackets. Required coverage: [R37] immutability — reference identity (toBe) for no-op paths: reveal on revealed/flagged cell, toggleFlag on revealed cell, chord on non-qualifying cell, any call after won/lost; deep-freeze input before mutating calls to catch in-place mutation. [R38] RangeError boundaries: rows<5, cols>50, mines=0, mines=rows*cols-8 (max+1). [R39] layout fixes board exactly, ignores provided rows/cols/mines options; size rule still applies. [R40] first-click safety with fixed layout — revealed cell and all 8 neighbours have mine:false; pre-reveal cells all adjacent:0 mine:false; same seed + first cell yields identical boards. [R41] status transitions: ready→playing on first reveal, →lost on mine, →won when all non-mines revealed; terminal states return same object reference. [R42] flood-fill: zero-cell region reveals connected neighbours, numbered border cells revealed but not expanded; flagged cells never revealed by flood; lastRevealed distances correct via BFS through zero-cells only (test with hand-built layout so region shape is known). [R43] loss: revealing a mine reveals every mine, flags stay in place. [R6] win: every mine has flagged:true after win. [R7] toggleFlag on hidden cell toggles correctly; on revealed cell returns same object. [R8] chord: correct flag count reveals unflagged neighbours with flood; wrong flag loses game; non-qualifying chord is no-op returning same object; lastRevealed distance from chorded cell (0 for it). [R9] minesLeft = mines - flagged, can be negative (flag 5 cells with mines=3, assert minesLeft === -2). [R35/R36] engine exports are pure (no DOM imports), type shapes match spec. Use fixed layouts (rule 3) for all deterministic tests — no random seeds in assertions.
